lesson: Byte-mirror resync inherits fresh-side content losses: v10 H1 rewrite of WALTEUR-builder-CLAUDE.md silently dropped per-discipline plan-review (gstack); cp propagated loss to walteur/SKILL.md. Rule: before declaring old side a strict subset, grep CHANGELOG-documented features against the survivor, not just diff hunks. Caught by adversarial verifier vs pre-copy snapshot; restored 2026-07-03.

Rollup/summary entries drop items silently even when written carefully: S016 vanished from a 34-entry CHANGELOG rollup whose OWN THEME was catching silent content loss. Rule: before shipping any rollup, enumerate source IDs mechanically (grep count) and assert N-of-N coverage; a theme-grouped narrative is not proof of coverage. Second instance of the summarizer-drop class this campaign (first: mirror-resync per-discipline plan-review).

Drift sweeps must grep the CLASS pattern (e.g. [0-9]+ gates), never the known-bad instances (120/137): a 125-gates claim survived a sweep that only searched the two numbers the panel had flagged. Third summarizer/sweep-drop instance this campaign.

Verification probes written for bash silently false-pass under zsh: zsh does not word-split $PATH in for-loops, so a PATH-filter shim removed nothing and the jq-absent probe reported PASS. Run shell probes under bash -c explicitly. The fix was fine; the probe lied.

Bulk file rewrites (python write_text, jq>tmp+mv, sync tools) can leave .sh files without exec bits; selftests that re-invoke via "$0" then fail rc=126 on EVERY case, and [ -x ] guards report runners missing. 217 walteur-kit .sh files were non-executable. After any bulk rewrite: /usr/bin/find <tree> -name "*.sh" ! -perm -u+x -exec chmod +x {} + . Also: run the aggregate suite BEFORE a bulk change to own a baseline.

Fixer self-reports understate diff scope (twice now: mirror-resync claimed 4 strings was 12; B28 claimed no-other-file while gate-registry.json changed). Rule: fixer reports must attach the working-tree diff --stat output verbatim; verifiers ALWAYS recompute scope from the tree, never from the report.

gitleaks detect in history-mode on a tree without VCS metadata is BLIND (scans nothing, exits 0 = false-green on real secrets) or errors (which the gate then misreported as secrets detected). Gates certifying a build TREE must scan files (the file-mode flag) and separate findings (custom exit code 9) from tool errors. Also: synthetic negative-control payloads must pass the scanner entropy/allowlist filters — use a proven-detectable literal.

BSD `date -j -f "%Y-%m-%d" "$d"` fills unspecified H:M:S with the CURRENT time, not midnight — two bare-date parses seconds apart race a second boundary, so a same-day date intermittently reads "in the future" (~15% flake). Pin midnight: -f "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S" "$d 00:00:00".

macOS `mktemp "PREFIX.XXXXXX.json"` FAILS deterministically (mkstemp: File exists / Operation not permitted) — BSD mktemp requires the X-run at the END of the template; a suffix after the Xs is illegal. Never put an extension after XXXXXX; use "PREFIX.XXXXXX" and the path is still fine for jq.

ship-gate exports WALTEUR_TOOLGATE_STRICT=1 on a real ship, flipping tool-backed gates (knip/medusa/lighthouse) to fail-closed when the tool is absent — you CANNOT override it from outside (it re-exports). A synthetic selftest fixture with JS/TS sources but no scanners installed must scope-bypass the specific tool-gates (WALTEUR_DEADCODE/SECSCAN/MEASURED_QUALITY=off), same pattern as WALTEUR_PERF=off.

od piped to awk emits a trailing empty line, so `od -An -tu1 -jN -N4 | awk {print $1..$4}` yields a TWO-line value (e.g. "1
0") that breaks a later `[ "$v" -lt X ]` integer test (silently evaluates false -> check no-ops). Pin to the first complete record: `awk NF>=4{print ...; exit}`.
source: harness-100 loop, B31 png dimension check reverse-test

lesson: A doctor/triage pointer that emits REMEDIATION.md#<report.gate> silently dangles when the report .gate is a SHORT id (anti-slop-code) but the doc header is the registry slug (## anti-slop-code-gate) — 69/91 links were dead. Resolve the anchor against the ACTUAL headers (try <id>, <id>-gate, <id>-lint, <id>-check; honest bare-id fallback), and lock it with a selftest that asserts resolution. Never emit a cross-ref id without checking the target exists.

The flagship SKILL.md claimed a WIRED self-improvement loop citing lesson-feedback.sh --drain, reflect.sh, conflicts.jsonl, retired.jsonl, pending-feedback.jsonl + lesson-gate dedupe/contradiction-hold as (proven) — NONE existed and the hook header explicitly disclaims dedupe. A doc that describes a design as SHIPPED must be checked against the filesystem: verify each cited file/capability exists before writing WIRED/proven. Mark unbuilt parts ROADMAP, not covered.

A tool-gate that fail-closes only under its OWN local strict flag (WALTEUR_OSV=strict) does NOT fire at ship time — ship-gate exports the GLOBAL WALTEUR_TOOLGATE_STRICT=1, so a can-not-verify loud-skips to exit 0 during a real ship. Every scanner gate must escalate on ${LOCAL_STRICT:-${WALTEUR_TOOLGATE_STRICT:-0}}, guarding that the DEFAULT-on mode escalates while an explicit =off bypass still wins.

A gate whose --help advertises --selftest but has no selftest() is a hollow claim (remediation-coverage-gate C2 only checks --help EXISTS, not that --selftest works). When adding a selftest to a tool-gate, force the tool-absent/present conditions via a BASE-ONLY PATH (symlink just bash/jq/find/... into a temp bin, run under env -i PATH=that) so the result is host-independent — otherwise a machine that happens to have trivy/hadolint installed gives different verdicts than a bare CI box.

A tool that resolves its store as ${ENV_VAR:-$HOME/default} silently ignores a co-located PROJECT store: lesson-gate default freshness read ~/.walteur/memory and WARNed no-store while 15 real lessons sat in walteur-kit/memory. When an explicit override is unset, prefer a co-located project store if it exists before the per-user default — a default run should find the repo own state, not misreport empty.
source: harness-100 loop, panel-3 memory gap B43

lesson: A core hook can be fully BROKEN on a platform yet invisible if it is not in the aggregate suite. stamp.sh (STAMP.md score recorder) parsed the gate-suite ts with GNU-only `date -d`, which fails on BSD/macOS, so it REFUSED every stamp — and because stamp.sh was never wired into selftest.sh, its 13/19 selftest failure was never surfaced. Two fixes needed: the BSD `-j -f` date fallback (same class as the 6 bare-date heals), AND wiring the gate into the aggregate so a regression cannot hide again. When a gate has a --selftest, assert it in the aggregate.

jq strptime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z") CANNOT parse a +00:00 (colon) timezone on macOS libc — it wants +0000. Converting Z->+00:00 then strptime silently fails, so a freshness check treats EVERY ts-bearing report as unparseable/stale. Use jq fromdateiso8601 for ISO-8601 Z timestamps (portable, built-in) instead of sub+strptime+mktime. This false-FAILed execution-ratio-gate on every macOS ship run.

A gate can have a passing-LOOKING --selftest yet be fully BROKEN if the aggregate never runs it. The coverage META-check only required registry-SELECTED spec gates, leaving 24 gate-selftests un-asserted — which hid 3 real macOS breaks (stamp, stamp-integrity, execution-ratio). Sweep: grep every walteur-kit/hooks/*.sh with a --selftest dispatch, cross-ref against selftest.sh assertions, RUN each gap (failing = a hidden break), fix + wire ALL of them so no gate-with-selftest is un-covered.

Applying the class-sweep lesson is not enough — you must re-grep to confirm ZERO instances remain. In B48 I fixed one BSD `sed -i` (line 114) but missed its sibling (line 118) in the same file; a follow-up portability audit caught it. After any class fix, run the negative grep (`... | grep -vE <fixed-form> || echo CLEAN`) and assert CLEAN. The sweep is not done until the grep is empty.

To browser-proof a Vite/React build, serve dist/ over http (python3 -m http.server) and render via Playwright — do NOT load dist/index.html over file://: Vite emits <script type=module>, and ESM is CORS-blocked over file:// (blank page). browser-proof-gate needs a route with a non-empty id + path + browser + integer viewport + status:PASS + screenshot_ref/accessibility_ref/interaction_ref, and every referenced file must exist non-empty. Capture REAL Playwright screenshot+a11y-snapshot+a click-and-observe interaction, never placeholders.

UI-detecting gates (browser-proof/design/anti-slop-ui) that find *.tsx/*.html anywhere under the scan root will mis-classify a build-engine repo as a UI product: they scan into eval FIXTURES (walteur-kit/eval-harness/slop-ui), GENERATED output (graphify-out/graph.html), and self-contained SUB-PROJECTS (field-runs/*/). Prune */walteur-kit/*, */graphify-out/*, and "$ROOT/field-runs/*" (anchored to the scan root, NOT */field-runs/* — the latter would prune a field-run scanned directly). Adding a real UI field-run surfaced this latent repo-root false-FAIL. Verify-by-refutation on your OWN change catches these.
source: harness-100 loop, B51 (surfaced by B50 design field-run)

lesson: ci-hardening-gate flags actions/checkout steps missing persist-credentials:false in their with block (GITHUB_TOKEN persists on disk for later steps to exfiltrate). Every checkout in every .github/workflows/*.yml needs a with block setting persist-credentials to false. Found 2 in twin-invariant.yml. When adding a new workflow job, always include it. The gate is ADVISORY (non-blocking) so these silently accumulate — audit it real-file, not just --selftest.

evidence-bundle self-consistency: a proof bundle that cites an artifact (a11y tree, screenshot) from a DIFFERENT build is an integrity crack a blind panel WILL catch even when every gate is green. Regenerate the artifact from the real render (never hand-write it), and harden the gate to assert app-specific markers so a stale cross-app artifact FAILs.
why: panel #5 caught a stale a11y snapshot of a different app inside the B50 Cadence proof; fixed by live re-render + a per-route evidence_must_contain check in browser-proof-gate

lesson: A gated fix often has a non-gated twin: the memory recall floor was parked behind walteur.js (gated), but the global store it reads is HOME, not gated. Project the canonical co-located corpus INTO the path the gated reader reads, rather than edit the gated reader.

A HARD gate crafted only with true-positive fixtures can hide false-POSITIVES on legit code (DOM .replaceWith(), a : any type annotation, prose to do / a Todo product name). When tightening a detection regex, reverse-test a MATRIX: every FP case must stop matching AND every TP case must stay caught (zero false-negative), then add BOTH as durable fixtures. Case-sensitivity frees UPPERCASE-acronym false positives without weakening detection when paired with a colon-anchored lowercase catch.

release-ledger schema requires current_version to appear in aggregate_history (any(.aggregate_history[]; .version==current_version)). So EVERY version bump needs a matching history row, even a no-count-change correctness fix where expected_passed repeats. Skipping it FAILs release-ledger-lint ledger-shape (schema floor), not the B33 count cross-check.

When building a COMPUTED quality metric, pick false-positive-SAFE invariants over plausible-but-FP-risky ones. For a type scale, check monotonicity+distinctness (a scale SHOULD strictly increase) and an AUTHOR-DECLARED base grid, NOT a constant modular ratio - a legit hybrid scale (tight UI steps + big display jump, 12/13/15/17/20/28/64) must pass. Same class as the anti-slop FP trap. Also: a computed gate that finds no defect in the current flagship is still genuine (enforcement going forward), but record HONESTLY that it found nothing (unlike a defect-fix).

When verifying a surprising gate finding, isolate the SPECIFIC check, not the exit code. A secret-scan FN in .mjs was masked twice: first by a missing policy (NOT_APPLICABLE exit 0), then by an incomplete policy (baseline violations made ALL extensions exit 2). Only by reading findings[].check (committed_secret fires for .js NOT .mjs) did the real blind spot surface. Exit code alone lies when other violations co-fire. Root cause: a secret-scanner file-extension allowlist that omits .mjs/.cjs/.mts/.cts silently skips modern ES-module source.

A gate that trusts a SELF-REPORTED manifest is decoupled from ground truth - you can declare fake passing values while shipping failing source (design-contrast-gate PASSED on a manifest whose colors were not in the CSS). Close it with a drift cross-check: verify each declared value ACTUALLY APPEARS in the real artifact (RGB-normalized with tolerance so format differences do not false-FAIL), active only when the artifact exists. Same class as the browser-proof stale-snapshot crack. Do NOT auto-extract (B65) - just VERIFY presence, which is tractable and correct.

Fixing a tool-absence fail-OPEN in ONE gate does not fix siblings with the same pattern. B62 fixed anti-slop-code-gate to fail-CLOSED at ship (WALTEUR_TOOLGATE_STRICT) when perl is absent, but secret-rotation-gate had the IDENTICAL hole unfixed - at ship with perl/jq absent it SKIPped exit 0, so a committed AKIA in a HARD secrets-never-committed gate slipped through. When you fix a fail-open class in one gate, SWEEP every tool-dependent gate for the same class. Also: a substring credential pattern (changeme) false-positives on identifiers (exchangeMessage) - use a LEADING word boundary (bchangeme) to free identifiers while keeping suffixed placeholders (changeme123); a comment-marker scan must exclude URLs (// not preceded by colon).

Reading $? after a pipe reports the LAST command's status, not the one under test. Hit three times in one session: a gate's rc lost to `| head`; an impeccable exit code misread through `| tail`, which put a FALSE claim into a gate header that then had to be corrected; and it is the same defect that makes Ralph's loop unable to distinguish a crashed agent from a productive one. Rule: capture rc directly with no pipe, or use PIPESTATUS. Never document a third-party tool's exit contract from a piped measurement.

A child process that reads stdin inside a `while read < file` loop SWALLOWS THE REST OF THAT FILE. walteur-loop's first real sweep measured 18 of 59 pinned gates while the oracle reported confidently on the partial set. An under-measured denominator is a false-GREEN path -- the worst bug class possible in a completion oracle. Fix: invoke children with </dev/null, read the driver file on FD 3, and assert measured-count == declared-count, dying rather than emitting a partial result.

gate-registry.json's `report` field can name a file the hook never writes, making the gate UNOBSERVABLE. Found in 3 of 148 gates, one HARD (mutation-gate, whose hook deliberately separates an INPUT manifest from its own verdict output). 145 of 148 agreed, and that near-universality is what proved `report` means 'the hook's own verdict file' and the 3 outliers were bugs rather than intent. Verified by deleting the declared file, running the hook, and re-checking.

A org-goal state file parked in a project _agent_state/ is invisible to /goal, which scans only the vault. THREE goals accumulated for one outcome before the collision surfaced. Two compounding causes: OneDrive dehydration made the files read as 0 bytes while stat showed real size, and a deadline of the literal string 'rolling' disabled every drift and expiry check for 35 days. Fix: vault copy authoritative, project copy a declared byte-identical mirror; on scan, stat-size > readable-bytes means UNREADABLE not absent; non-ISO deadline refused at capture; off-enum status fails loudly.

macOS ships /bin/bash 3.2, where `mapfile` does not exist. Under set -u it fails with 'mapfile: command not found' then 'unbound variable', returning rc=1 -- a gate that neither passes nor fails. Every hook in this kit must run on stock macOS bash: use a temp file plus a plain while-read loop.

An audit that calls something junk must be verified before deletion. The 2026-07-24 structural audit listed _agent_state/ and graphify-out/ as DELETE-JUNK; the first holds the campaign's own goal state and the second IS m5's verification artifact. 4 of 5 remaining delete candidates also had real references in README/SKILL.md/selftest.sh. Rule: prove every delete target is both untracked AND reference-free, and re-read the target rather than trusting the audit's label.

A `git push` that prints 'To <url>' and 'old..new  main -> main' is NOT proof the remote ref moved. Pushes of two repos printed exactly that and updated the local remote-tracking refs, while `git ls-remote origin` showed the remote still at the old commit and a 'new branch' absent entirely. Re-pushing landed them, and the second push reported '[new branch]' for a branch the first claimed to have created. Confirm every push with `git ls-remote origin <ref>`; the remote-tracking ref is local state.

A GitHub Actions workflow can be committed, correct, and never executed. On a private repo with an exhausted Actions budget every run is a failure with ZERO steps and the annotation 'The job was not started because an Actions budget is preventing further use.' Both repos were in that state for their whole history while their docs described CI as enforcing gates. Confirm with `gh run list` plus the run annotations; reading the YAML proves only that it is declared.

A verification step that prints nothing and exits 0 has almost certainly not run. refresh-fixture-dates.sh --verify called `main write >/dev/null`; a redirection on a function call is not a subshell, so main's closing `exit 0` ended the script before a single twin ran. It was wired into CI in that state and its own fail-closed twin-count guard never fired. Assert on the OUTPUT of a verification step, never only on its exit code.

Git cannot re-include a file whose PARENT DIRECTORY is excluded, so `!path/**/node_modules/**` is inert while `**/node_modules/` stands. Negate the directory first, then the contents, and keep both lines LAST so no later pattern re-excludes them. An inert negation looks like a working guard until something exercises it, and `git add -f` masks it further. Prove negations with `git add -An` or `git check-ignore -v`.

`${path%%/seg/*}` strips from the FIRST occurrence of /seg/, `${path%/seg/*}` from the LAST. An adopted tree carries TWO /walteur-kit/ segments, so `%%` returned the repo root instead of the fixture directory: no offset marker was found and the 14-day-edge fixture was silently re-dated to today, off the threshold it exists to sit on. Green in the standalone layout, wrong in the real one. Selftest every path-parsing helper in BOTH layouts it will run in.

A mutation-testing harness must run a semantically-null mutant per target FIRST and require it to reproduce that target's own baseline, excluding any target that fails the control and failing closed. Two defects in gate-mutation.sh (mutants staged outside the hooks dir so sibling sourcing broke, and a CR-sensitive no-op guard that skipped nothing) both produced verdicts unrelated to the mutation and forced a public retraction of the numbers. One null control would have caught both on the first run.
